land.text: Dakshina Kosala, whose capital Shripura 'had also served as the capital of the preceding Sharabhapuriya kings'

predecessors.note: Infobox 'Preceded by: Sharabhapuriya dynasty'. The page says the Panduvamshis 'did not immediately succeed the Sharabhapuriyas', whose rule 'ended sometime around 590 CE'. No dossier for the Sharabhapuriyas exists yet.

land.text: Bastar and Koraput, the Nala core

predecessors.note: Listed only because the Nala dossier names this dynasty as its successor (Nala page: the Nalas 'were probably supplanted by the Panduvamshi dynasty'); the Dakshina Kosala page does not say so and has the territory 'subsequently ruled by the Nalas, the Banas and the Kalachuris'. No event here draws it.

land.text: Kosala in western Odisha, the land the Somavamshi dossier takes over from the Panduvamshis

successors.note: Infobox 'Succeeded by: Somavamshi dynasty'; the Somavamshis 'appear to have been related' to the Panduvamshis, which 'cannot be said with certainty'. The page has 'no record of Panduvamshis after Balarjuna' (r. c. 730-790) while the Somavamshi dossier starts c. 882, so about ninety years lie between; the land is nobody's on the map until then.

capitals.name: Shripura (Sirpur)
capitals.note: Infobox capital 'Sirpur, Mahasamund'; 'The capital of the dynasty was most probably located at Shripura', which 'had also served as the capital of the preceding Sharabhapuriya kings'. No years; the dynasty's span is used. The gazetteer has no Sirpur; the coordinates are approximate.

rulers.name: Indrabala
rulers.note: Reign years follow Shastri's chronology as the page gives them ('r. c. 620-640 CE'); Udayana, 'r. c. 600-620 CE', is the earliest king in the inscriptions but 'probably did not rule Dakshina Kosala'.

rulers.name: Tivaradeva (Mahashiva Tivara)
rulers.note: 'r. c. 660-680 CE'; his inscriptions call him Kosaladhipati. The date is disputed: Mirashi and Sircar placed him in the 6th century, Cunningham proposed 425-450 CE.

rulers.name: Nannaraja II (Nanna II)
rulers.note: 'r. c. 680-700 CE'; may have extended the kingdom to Vidarbha, for how long is undetermined.

rulers.name: Balarjuna (Mahashivagupta)
rulers.note: 'r. c. 730-790 CE'; 'There is no record of Panduvamshis after Balarjuna'.

correction.text: Dakshina Kosala, the Mahanadi plain round Shripura (Sirpur): the page names the region, not its limits

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (no Cliopatria row; no Cliopatria polity of Dakshina Kosala exists in this period). The page gives no area and no boundary: Tivaradeva is 'Kosaladhipati', his control of 'other regions such as Utkala did not last long', and Nannaraja II 'may have expanded' to Vidarbha. The 150 km disc round Raipur (about 70,000 km2) stands for the Chhattisgarh plain with Sirpur 60 km to the north-east of it; Utkala and Vidarbha are not drawn.

region.text: Dakshina Kosala, 'the region was conquered by his descendants' (Udayana's)

ledger.note: c. 620: the Panduvamshis rule Dakshina Kosala from Shripura. Infobox 'Established: c. 7th century CE'; Udayana (r. c. 600-620) 'probably did not rule Dakshina Kosala, and the region was conquered by his descendants', so the first reign that can have held it, Indrabala's (c. 620-640), is the bridge. The Sharabhapuriya rule 'ended sometime around 590 CE' and the Panduvamshis 'did not immediately succeed' them. Reviewer (2026-11-01): the page itself says 'Shastri dates the beginning of the Panduvamshi rule in Dakshina Kosala to c. 620 CE', so the year is the page's and the region the reading (confidence 2).

c. 790 (bridging year): the Panduvamshi line ends in Dakshina Kosala. 'There is no record of Panduvamshis after Balarjuna' (r. c. 730-790) and 'their rule in Dakshina Kosala probably ended in the 8th century'; infobox 'disestablished: c. 8th century CE'. The page says the territory was 'subsequently ruled by the Nalas, the Banas and the Kalachuris' without dates; the Somavamshi dossier starts c. 882.

certainty.note: No boundary is given; the kingdom is a radius round Raipur for the Mahanadi plain, and the reign years are the page's 'c.' chronology (Shastri's), disputed for Tivaradeva.

sources.title: Panduvamshis of Dakshina Kosala
sources.note: Identity, infobox c. 7th to c. 8th century, capital Shripura/Sirpur, ruler chronology, territory (Kosala, Utkala, Vidarbha), end after Balarjuna. The article carries no war and no dated conquest.

sources.title: Somavamshi dynasty
sources.note: Read for the link to the Somavamshis: kinship 'cannot be said with certainty', Panduvamshi rule 'seems to have declined in the 8th century', one theory of expulsion by the Kalachuris and a move east to Vinitapura (Binka); Janmejaya I c. 882-922. No dated event.

notes: Two pages opened; the dynasty's article is thin and dates only reigns, in Shastri's c. chronology. 'panduvamshi-dynasty' is the Panduvamshis of Dakshina Kosala (Sirpur, Chhattisgarh); the Wikipedia article also refers to an earlier Panduvamshi line of Mekala ('an earlier dynasty that ruled an adjacent area') whose relation is uncertain, and no dossier exists for it. Cross-links: the Nala dossier lists this dynasty as the Nalas' successor (Bastar and Koraput) c. 580 on the Nala page's 'probably supplanted'; the Dakshina Kosala page does not say so, and a gap-filler should read the Nala page. The Somavamshi dossier lists it as predecessor (Sambalpur, 882). The Somavamshi page (opened) says only that 'according to one theory, the Panduvamshis were driven out of Kosala by the Kalachuris, and migrated eastward' and 'established their capital at Vinitapura (modern Binka) on the banks of the Mahanadi', that their rule in Dakshina Kosala 'seems to have declined in the 8th century' and that the Somavamshis 'may have been related' to them, all undated; the dynasty's own page ends it in the 8th century, so the land 790-882 is drawn as nobody's and a later Binka line of 'later Panduvamshis' is not drawn. The Sharabhapuriya dynasty has no dossier. The Somavamshi dossier calls the founder of Kosala rule 'Janmejaya I'; the Panduvamshi page names Nannadeva/Mahabhavagupta/Yayati nowhere. Gazetteer: no Sirpur/Mahasamund/Dakshina Kosala entries. Wikidata id left null.
